title: Three-time DPOY Aaron Donald unretiring to play for Rams
content:
It turns out the Los Angeles Rams had one more blockbuster in them.

Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald is returning to play for the Rams. More than two years after his retirement, Donald is returning at age 35. Donald is attempting something rarely done for a player in his mid-30s multiple seasons away from the game, but this is a situation that has been building steam for months now.

It started when the Rams made the blockbuster trade in May to acquire reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns. Rams coach Sean McVay had a call with Donald about the idea of bringing in Garrett, and Donald has long been fascinated by the idea of sharing a defensive line with another superstar player, given the steady rate of double teams he had to face in his 10-year career.

Donald said when he visited the facility last fall that he did not have an interest in playing again, but this spring’s moves changed the circumstances. He has been working out regularly at the Rams facility, and he went through two workouts that the team reported to the league as official tryouts since training camp started.

“It didn’t feel like he missed a beat at all,” said Rams defensive lineman Desjuan Johnson, who joined Donald for a speed workout in August. “It feels like he even got a little bit faster, a little bit hungrier in a way.”

Now, the Rams will have two multi-time Defensive Players of the Year on the same defensive line. Donald has 111 career sacks in 10 seasons. Garrett has 125.5 in nine seasons.

Donald’s return completes the Rams’ defensive makeover this offseason. In addition to trading Jared Verse to land Garrett from the Browns, the Rams also pulled off a blockbuster trade with the Kansas City Chiefs for two-time All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson to start at the other outside cornerback spot. Those moves came after Matthew Stafford returned for an 18th NFL season, fresh off his first MVP trophy.

Now, the Rams will have a defensive line featuring Garrett, Donald, Byron Young off a 12-sack Pro Bowl season and Kobie Turner off a seven-sack campaign. Those four will get to mix and match alignments and on stunts and games in defensive coordinator Chris Shula’s creative scheme.

“Are there so many things we could do in terms of pressures and blitzes and all of that stuff? Of course,” safety and captain Quentin Lake said this spring. “That’s unheard of, to have two guys who won Defensive Player of the Year on the same team. It would be one fun year, I’ll say that.”

The push for a Super Bowl after a narrow loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game spoke to Donald. And now, the Rams hope they can do what they did with Donald in 2021, when they hoisted the Lombardi Trophy after winning the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium.
